models.strictJsonSchema: Yes on Chat Completions: the structured-outputs guide says strict:true 'uses constrained decoding' on gpt-oss-20b, gpt-oss-120b, qwen3.8-27b and muse-spark-open. Strict mode requires every property to be required and additionalProperties:false; the project schema already enforces both. Documented: string, number, boolean, integer, object, array, enum, anyOf (each branch held to the same rules), null through a type union such as ["string","null"], $defs/$ref and recursion. Not documented: const (string or number) and minimum/maximum. The only official example that uses minimum/maximum runs in best-effort mode, not strict. Streaming and tool use cannot be combined with Structured Outputs. Responses API: POST https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/responses (beta). Its OpenAPI spec defines text.format {type:'json_schema', name, schema, strict}. The examples there omit strict, so it is not stated that strict on /responses triggers the same constrained decoding.

The documented Responses output contains a 'reasoning' item with plaintext content [{type:'reasoning_text'}], and recordedResponse.ts in this repo rejects plaintext reasoning items as unsupported, so the existing parser would mark every call non-actionable.

models.strictJsonSchema: Partial or unverified. Chat Completions response_format supports only text or json_object, with no schema enforcement, and the docs warn the API 'may occasionally return empty content'. The Responses API (POST https://api.deepseek.com/responses) reference lists text.format type json_schema with name and schema 'for structured output conforming to the given JSON Schema', and the compatibility table says 'format fully supported'. There is no 'strict' field, no supported-keyword list and no mention of constrained decoding, and 'Unsupported parameters are silently ignored'. Separately, tool calls have a strict mode (beta, base_url /beta) in which the server validates the schema. That mode documents object, string, number, integer, boolean, array, enum, anyOf and $ref/$def, and const, minimum and maximum on numbers only. It does not list type null or const on strings, and does not support minLength/maxLength/minItems/maxItems.
models.reasoningControl: Thinking is on by default. Responses API: reasoning.effort 'none' disables it; low/high/max are accepted, and minimal/low both map to low. Chat API: thinking {type: enabled|disabled} and reasoning_effort. The transport currently sends effort 'low', which keeps thinking ON. In thinking mode the reasoning text is returned and would trip the parser's plaintext-reasoning rejection.
models.cheaperTiers: Off-peak pricing is half of peak. Peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC, Monday to Friday, and everything else is off-peak. Off-peak rates: input $0.15/M, cache hit $0.003/M, output $0.60/M. The prices in the fields above are peak. No batch tier is listed.
models.deprecation: Pinning is not possible. Only the aliases deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro exist, and the docs say 'legacy names deepseek-v4-flash ... are still accepted, but the corresponding models have been retired; their requests are served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017'. The weights are open-sourced (Hugging Face deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017).

models.strictJsonSchema: Yes, constrained during generation: the docs say the schema is 'enforced during generation' and that Grammar mode is available. Documented: types string, number, integer, boolean, object, array and null; properties/required/additionalProperties; items; minLength/maxLength/minItems/maxItems; pattern; anyOf/allOf/oneOf; $defs/definitions with $ref, including recursion. Properties are treated as unevaluatedProperties:false. Caveat: pattern is 'best-effort', and constructs that cannot be compiled are 'safely ignored', so constraints can be silently relaxed. enum, const, minimum and maximum are not mentioned. Responses API: POST https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1/responses documents text.format {type:'json_schema', name, strict:true, schema} ('Constrain output to a JSON schema').
models.reasoningControl: reasoning.effort is supported. 'reasoning.summary is not configurable — summaries are always included when the model produces reasoning content'. The current parser rejects reasoning items that have a non-empty summary.

models.deprecation: Serverless models 'may be updated or deprecated', with at least 2 weeks' notice. Fireworks recommends on-demand deployments for version control.

Most important finding: no candidate is a drop-in replacement for the current transport, even where the provider offers /v1/responses with text.format json_schema strict. In the repo, (1) src/agent/responsesTransport.ts hard-codes https://api.openai.com/v1/responses and requires the pathname '/v1/responses'. The provider paths differ: Groq /openai/v1/responses, Fireworks /inference/v1/responses, OpenRouter /api/v1/responses, DeepSeek /responses, Alibaba /compatible-mode/v1/responses. (2) The model-ID check in src/agent/responsesRequest.ts (/^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}$/) rejects '/', so openai/gpt-oss-120b and accounts/fireworks/models/... fail; deepseek-flash passes. (3) src/agent/recordedResponse.ts deliberately rejects reasoning items that carry plaintext content or a non-empty summary. Groq returns {type:'reasoning', content:[{type:'reasoning_text'}]} for gpt-oss, which has no effort 'none'. Fireworks always includes reasoning summaries. DeepSeek thinking is on unless reasoning.effort is 'none', and the request currently sends 'low'. These are configuration and parser changes rather than a new protocol adapter, but they touch the accounting and containment boundary. Do not change them without a deliberate decision.

Best-verified strict path: Groq, whose docs say outright that strict:true uses constrained decoding, for gpt-oss-120b ($0.15/$0.60 per M), gpt-oss-20b ($0.075/$0.30) and qwen3.8-27b (preview, $0.80/$4.00). Gaps: const and minimum/maximum are not in Groq's documented strict subset, and the project schema (src/agent/mockProvider.ts) uses string const, number const, nested anyOf, null and minimum/maximum (bakerPrice 0-2). That combination must be probed before any study run.

Mistral (strict flag accepted, enforcement undocumented) and Together (constrained decoding described, but no strict flag or keyword list) offer no Responses API, so each would need a Chat Completions adapter.

DeepSeek official is the cheapest large model ($0.30/$1.20 peak, $0.15/$0.60 off-peak), but schema enforcement is undocumented: Chat Completions supports json_object only, the Responses json_schema has no strict field and unsupported parameters are 'silently ignored'. The model cannot be pinned, because legacy names are silently served by the newest Flash. Dated third-party IDs exist: Fireworks deepseek-v4p1-flash-1017 at $0.30/$0.006/$1.20, Together deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at the same price, and OpenRouter deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017. On OpenRouter the DeepSeek first-party endpoint reports structured_outputs=false.

Llama: Groq announced the deprecation of llama-3.1-8b-instant and llama-3.3-70b-versatile with shutdown on 08/16/26, recommending gpt-oss-20b and gpt-oss-120b. Its models page now lists both as Enterprise / Contact Sales. No Llama entry is recommended.

Data terms at a glance (stated on official pages): Groq does not retain inference data by default, apart from up to 30 days of reliability/abuse logs; ZDR is self-serve and data is stored in US GCP. Fireworks has zero retention by default, but /responses stores data for 30 days when store=true, which is its default; the transport sends store:false. OpenRouter stores no prompts unless the user opts in, and its Responses API rejects store:true. Together stores prompts and outputs by default for product improvement, with training opt-in off by default and ZDR as a toggle. Mistral offers ZDR on paid plans plus a separate training opt-out whose default is unstated. DeepSeek's privacy policy was unreachable, and its terms do not address training.

Illustrative study-1 cost, arithmetic only and not a quote: assuming ~7,000 input and ~500 output tokens including reasoning, 630 calls cost about $0.85 on Groq gpt-oss-120b, $0.43 on gpt-oss-20b, $1.70 on DeepSeek Flash at peak ($0.85 off-peak) and $0.78 on Mistral Small 4, before the project's 2x conservative booking. Cache hits would lower these figures.
Batch tiers (Groq, Fireworks, OpenRouter :batch; Groq's window is 24h-7d) are not usable for sequential 16-second ticks. Groq flex costs the same as on-demand but can fail fast with HTTP 498.
